name: Mahlah
overview: Mahlah was a female member of the tribe of Manasseh, known specifically as a daughter of Zelophehad. Her identity is grounded primarily in this familial connection, as recorded in Numbers 26:33. Beyond this, Scripture does not provide additional personal details or notes about her life.
namesAndTitles: The name Mahlah is a proper name mentioned in Numbers 26:33 and is possibly understood to mean 'weak one.' There is no indication that this name was given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Mahlah as a daughter of Zelophehad. No other family relationships are recorded beyond this connection.
scriptureSignificance: Mahlah's significance in the biblical narrative stems from her identification as a daughter of Zelophehad within the tribe of Manasseh. This connection places her within the context of Israel's tribal structure and inheritance discussions found in the Pentateuch. Although limited information is provided, her mention preserves the legacy of Zelophehad's family line.
